case_studies.title: Concurrency without Model Changes: Future-based Asynchronous Function Calling for LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Function calling, also known as tool use, is a core capability of modern LLM agents but is typically constrained by synchronous execution semantics. Under these semantics, LLM decoding is blocked until each function call completes, resulting in increasing end-to-end latency. In this work, we introduce AsyncFC, a pure execution-layer framework that decouples LLM decoding from function execution, enabling overlap between model decoding and function execution as well as inter-function parallelism when dependencies permit. AsyncFC layers over existing models and unmodified function implementations
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of synchronous execution in Large Language Models (LLMs) by introducing a framework called AsyncFC, which enables asynchronous function calling without requiring model changes. The result is improved performance with reduced end-to-end latency. This framework allows for overlap between model decoding and function execution, enabling parallelism when dependencies permit.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM-based systems, here is what to do: check if your current implementation uses synchronous execution, consider integrating AsyncFC to enable asynchronous function calling, and test for improved performance and reduced latency.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While this paper introduces an interesting asynchronous framework for LLMs, its direct relevance to IT engineers and consultants is relatively low. However, it could potentially enable faster deployment and automation of LLM-based systems, making it worth a relatively high novelty score. Value of the paper is low because its application in real-world infrastructure is abstract and requires further research

case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable abilities in reasoning. However, maximizing their potential through inference-time scaling faces challenges in trade-off between sampling budget and reasoning quality. Current strategies remain inefficient as they typically treat sampling width and depth as orthogonal objectives, where width consensus methods risk reinforcing hallucinations, while depth pruning mechanisms prematurely truncate complex yet valid reasoning chains. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of balancing budget and quality in Adaptive Inference-Time Scaling for Large Language Models. The authors built a framework called Dual-Dimensional Consistency (DDC) that bridges path quality with sampling budget. The result is a more efficient and effective way to scale LLMs.

case_studies.title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
case_studies.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Model (LLM) agents have enabled complex agentic workflows where models autonomously retrieve information, call tools, and reason over large corpora to complete tasks on behalf of users. Despite the growing adoption of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in agentic search systems, existing literature lacks a systematic comparison of how retrieval strategy choice interacts with agent architecture and tool-calling paradigm. It solves the problem of optimizing retrieval-augmented generation in agentic search systems. case_studies.title: Agentic AI in Industry: Adoption Level and Deployment Barriers
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems are entering software engineering workflows, yet empirical evidence on how industrial organizations actually adopt them remains sparse. We present a qualitative interview study with sixteen practitioners across twelve companies of varying size and domain. This study characterizes the current agentic AI adoption state of these companies, employing a six-level maturity framework adapted from established AI-driven organizations. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how companies adopt Agentic AI systems by building a maturity framework to assess their adoption levels, resulting in a better understanding of the current state of AI adoption in industries. The study found that most companies are at the early stages of AI adoption, with only one company at a more advanced level. This research provides insights into the challenges and barriers to AI adoption in industries.

case_studies.title: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints
case_studies.abstract: Deploying language models as autonomous agents requires more than per-task accuracy: when an agent faces a queue of problems under a finite token budget, it must decide which to attempt, in what order, and how much compute to commit to each, all before any execution feedback is available. This is the prospective form of metacognitive control studied for decades in human cognition, yet whether language models possess it remains untested. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of how language models can prioritize tasks and allocate resources when faced with a queue of problems and limited computing power. The authors built TRIAGE, an evaluation framework to test language models' ability to make these decisions. The result shows whether language models can possess prospective metacognitive control, but it's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Cattle Trade: A Multi-Agent Benchmark for LLM Bluffing, Bidding, and Bargaining
case_studies.abstract: We introduce \textsc{Cattle Trade, a multi-agent benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) as agents in strategic reasoning under imperfect information, adversarial interaction, and resource constraints. The benchmark combines auctions, hidden-offer trade challenges (TCs), bargaining, bluffing, opponent modeling, and resource allocation within a single long-horizon game lasting 50--60 turns. The Cattle Trade benchmark combines various economic and strategic challenges to assess the abilities of large language models. It is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.
